Australia first wore green and gold in 1899, when the Australian cricket team touring England adopted green and gold caps and blazers for the opening match of the Ashes series, arranged by captain Joe Darling [d1][d3][d8]. Prior to this, Australian teams had worn an assortment of club or state colours, including blue and white [d3]. In 1908, the Australian Board of Control for Cricket officially declared "gum-tree green and wattle gold" as the Australian cricket colours, and the Australasian Olympic team also appeared in green and wattle gold uniforms at the 1908 London Olympics [d1][d8]. While green and gold had been popularly embraced as Australia's sporting colours since the late 1800s, they were not formally proclaimed as the national colours until 19 April 1984, when Governor-General Sir Ninian Stephen made the official proclamation [d1][d5][d6].
